player.name: Wren Ashdown
player.concept: a quick-witted half-elf ranger with a longbow, a dry sense of humour and a soft spot for underdogs

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Late afternoon settles over the crossroads. The King’s Road meets a rutted track between tall blackthorn hedges; a weathered milestone stands beside a gibbet with nothing hanging from it. In the ditch, a dead ox lies with crude arrows in its flank. Crows watch from the posts while the wind brings the smell of woodsmoke from somewhere it shouldn’t.

A mud-caked farmer jabs his pitchfork at the hedge, then wheels on the milestone. “No, you don’t tell me where to stand, stone!” His eyes are red with exhaustion. He spots you and levels the pitchfork your way. “Stay back! I know what you are!”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I raise my hands and crouch so I am lower than his pitchfork. "Easy, friend. I am Wren. Whatever is in that hedge, I will see you home to your wife tonight. You have my word on it, and I keep my word."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The pitchfork dips, though Tam keeps both hands locked around its shaft. He studies your face, then your raised hands.

“Wren,” he repeats, as if testing whether the name has teeth. “Right. Right. You’ve got the look of someone who can see a hedge without blaming it on cider.”

His breath comes in a shudder. He glances at the blackthorn, where a few leaves stir though the air around you is still.

“Little green devils killed my ox last night. Been after me since dawn. I’m going home to Bet, and I don’t want them finding the farm.” He gives a thin, frightened laugh. “You said your word, then.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I take the last of my bread and the good wool scarf from my pack and press them into his hands. "Eat. And keep warm, you are shaking." Then I turn to the hedge. "You in there! I can hear you breathing. Come out and talk."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam clutches the bread and scarf to his chest. “You’re a good soul, Wren. Saints bless you and your turnips.” He bites into the bread at once, as if the hedge might object to the delay.

For a moment there’s only crows and the wind in the thorns. Then a thin voice from beyond the hedge answers, “Breathing? Skrag breathes like king! Longlegs, put bow down. Skrag wants talk.”

Tam goes grey beneath the sunburn. His hand strays to a small lump beneath his smock, then drops away. From the hedge comes the creak of a bow being drawn. “You give back Grandmother Bone,” the voice calls, “and Skrag takes little farmer away.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: "Tam. That bone thing under your smock. It is theirs, isnt it? Give it to me." I hold out my hand to him, then turn to the hedge. "Skrag! You will have your grandmother back. Bows down and nobody touches the farmer."

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Insight check to see what Tam is hiding: 10 + 3 = 13 vs DC 12: success

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam’s hand closes over the lump beneath his smock. You’ve caught him at it too many times for this to be a harmless farmer’s habit; he knows you’ve seen through him.

“Give it to you?” His voice cracks. “Finder’s keepers, Wren. Came up in my field. I was taking it to Caerwyn to sell. An ox like mine doesn’t grow on turnips.”

Still, after a frightened glance toward the hedge, he pulls the object free. It’s a little carved grandmother, old and unsettling, with garnets for eyes. It looks like a shrine figure, not something dug up for market. Tam keeps one hand around it, unwilling to let go.

From the hedge, Skrag gives a sharp little gasp. “Grandmother Bone! Longlegs, you have her!” A bowstring creaks. Tam flinches but doesn’t release the idol.

opened.title: Wren’s promise to get Tam home
